report.summary: The migration is complete: all 9 scripts reproduce the legacy Teradata outputs exactly on dataset A, and the reviewer has approved all 9. The inventory shows every script passing and approved, and I re-ran the comparison against the legacy output for each script myself. The converted SQL applies the legacy platform's rules everywhere they matter, not just where dataset A shows a difference. First, text comparisons ignore letter case and trailing spaces (Teradata session mode), including in joins, grouping, CASE tests and filters. Second, rounding sends halves to the even digit (RoundHalfwayMagUp=FALSE), done in exact decimal arithmetic. Third, integer division truncates. Fourth, NULLs sort first in ascending order and last in descending order. Fifth, TOP n WITH TIES is reproduced with RANK(). Where legacy behaviour looks wrong, it was kept for parity and recorded as a legacy-bug note. Nothing is hard-coded from the data, and run dates are read from etl_control.

traps: Session mode ignores case and trailing spaces, so the segment CASE compares UPPER(RTRIM(x,' ')) on both sides
ZEROIFNULL became COALESCE(credit_limit, 0)
INDEX became STRPOS on the uppercased email, keeping Teradata's case-insensitive search
TRIM removes only spaces, as in Teradata
The status IN test and the channel CASE tests are normalised with upper(rtrim(col,' ')) against the uppercased literal
Date minus date is cast to INTEGER
suspected_legacy_bugs: Every channel that isn't web or app, including kiosk and NULL, is mapped to 'store'

traps: CAST to DECIMAL(14,1) rounds halves to even on legacy; done explicitly in exact decimal arithmetic (checked on negative and large values)
Integer division truncates toward zero; done with exact integer division
suspected_legacy_bugs: avg_items_per_order uses integer division, so the fraction is dropped (affects 142 of 266 customers)

traps: Teradata sorts NULLs first in ascending order, DuckDB last; the QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER sort now says NULLS FIRST
suspected_legacy_bugs: Unshipped orders aren't excluded, so 117 of 266 customers get an unshipped order with a NULL ship date as their 'first fulfilment'

traps: The sku join between padded CHAR(10) order_lines.sku and products.sku normalises both sides with upper(rtrim())
MULTISET and PRIMARY INDEX were dropped because DuckDB has neither
Grouping by category ignores case and trailing spaces: rows are grouped on upper(rtrim(category)) and MIN(category) is shown as the spelling
yyyymm is an integer (year*100+month), revenue is DECIMAL(38,2)
TOP 10 WITH TIES became RANK() <= 10, ordered by order_cnt DESC NULLS LAST (28 rows on dataset A)
Date minus date is cast to INTEGER
run_date is read from etl_control as in legacy
A NULL date difference falls to ELSE 'LOW', the same on both platforms
suspected_legacy_bugs: first_order_unshipped really means 'has any unshipped order', inherited from first_fulfilment's NULLs-first sort
A customer with a NULL last_order_date is classed as LOW churn risk

traps: Segment change detection ignores case and trailing spaces
The is_current='Y' test ignores case in the join and the UPDATE, so lowercase 'y' rows count as current
run_date comes from etl_control; run_date - 1 and the end date DATE '9999-12-31' are handled as in legacy; the changed-customer list is built before the UPDATE, as in legacy
suspected_legacy_bugs: A segment change in case or trailing spaces only doesn't open a new version, and a NULL segment never counts as a change
A customer whose rows in yesterday's dimension are all closed is never reopened
Duplicate rows in stg_customers or several rows in etl_control would produce duplicate output rows

risks: s6: which original spelling Teradata shows when category names differing only in case or trailing spaces are grouped together is unconfirmed; MIN is assumed, and dataset A's categories are already uniform. Revenue and counts are unaffected; only the spelling in the output key could differ
s3: the half-even rounding assumes orders.amount keeps 2 decimal places (DECIMAL(12,2)); if the schema gains more decimal places, lifetime_value_1dp could quietly differ from legacy
s8 and s9 cross-join etl_control, so more than one row in it would duplicate customers on both platforms; that table must keep a single row
s7 can return more than 10 rows when there are ties (28 on dataset A); anything reading the table shouldn't assume 10
Cases dataset A doesn't cover are only checked against the logic: NULL names, emails without '@', duplicate normalised SKUs, several current rows per customer in dim_customer_prev
